questions.q: How does the root main.tf in this capstone use the azure-network and aws-network modules?
options: It calls only one of them, never both
It calls both modules side by side, each with its own configuration like a CIDR range
It copies their code directly into the root file
It calls them sequentially in separate Terraform runs
questions.explain: The root configuration calls both the azure_network and aws_network modules in the same main.tf, each with its own inputs like resource_group_name or vpc_cidr.

questions.q: What is the purpose of local.common_tags in this configuration?
options: It stores the Terraform state backend configuration
It defines one map of tags, reused by every resource, keeping tagging consistent without repeating it by hand
It is required by the azurerm provider to authenticate
It replaces the need for a .tfvars file
questions.explain: local.common_tags centralizes the tag values (like environment and project) so every resource references the same definition instead of duplicating it.

questions.q: How does the azurerm_service_plan resource get its resource group name, instead of hardcoding it?
options: It is typed directly as a literal string
It references module.azure_network.resource_group_name, a value the module exposes as an output
It is read from an environment variable
It queries the Azure Portal at runtime
questions.explain: The resource reads the resource group name from the azure_network module's output, demonstrating how a root module consumes a module's exposed values.

questions.q: What does the example terraform plan output 'Plan: 12 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy' indicate?
options: The plan failed with 12 errors
12 resources will be newly created, with nothing changed or destroyed — a clean plan matching expectations
12 resources already exist and will be deleted
The state file is corrupted
questions.explain: A plan summary of '12 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy' means the configuration will create 12 new resources cleanly, with no unexpected changes or deletions.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what should happen to this plan output before running terraform apply?
options: It should be applied immediately without review
It should be reviewed by a teammate in a pull request, per the CI/CD workflow from Chapter 7
It should be deleted and regenerated
It should be emailed to the cloud provider for approval
questions.explain: The lesson ties this back to Chapter 7's CI/CD pipeline, where a plan is reviewed by a teammate on a pull request before anything applies.
